paras.text: From 1206 to 1857 the rule of Muslims remained over the Subcontinent. During this the English gradually took possession of Hindustan. In 1857 the Hindus and Muslims together fought to expel the English from the country, which was given the name of the War of Independence, but it failed. The War of Independence of 1857 was an open display of the spirit of freedom of the Muslims. Because of defective organisation, shortage of resources and the absence of any united leader, the Muslims failed in this War of Independence. At this delicate time Sir Syed Ahmad Khan acquainted the Muslims of the Subcontinent with awareness and the light and importance of knowledge. He linked power with education and made this clear, that education is the only remedy for the economic, social and political wretched condition of Muslims. He made it clear that Muslims, only by being adorned with modern education, can get deliverance from the dominance of the English and the Hindus. He laid the foundation of the concept of a separate Islamic state. He prepared the Muslims of the Subcontinent to become united for the establishment of a separate Islamic state, so that all their affairs could be settled in the light of the Quran and Sunnah.

The movement, creation and political situation of Pakistan

The Pakistan Movement and the creation of Pakistan

In 711 CE, in the era of the Umayyad Caliph Walid bin Abd al-Malik, Muhammad bin Qasim (may Allah have mercy on him) attacked Sindh and conquered the Arab region, and thus the Subcontinent became part of the largest Arab state in the world, whose capital was Damascus, the language Arabic and the religion Islam. In this way this region became linked with the Arab world politically, religiously and culturally. This event left deep effects on the history of the Subcontinent and South Asia.

From 1206 to 1857 the rule of Muslims remained over the Subcontinent. During this the English gradually took possession of Hindustan. In 1857 the Hindus and Muslims together fought to expel the English from the country, which was given the name of the War of Independence, but it failed. The War of Independence of 1857 was an open display of the spirit of freedom of the Muslims. Because of defective organisation, shortage of resources and the absence of any united leader, the Muslims failed in this War of Independence. At this delicate time Sir Syed Ahmad Khan acquainted the Muslims of the Subcontinent with awareness and the light and importance of knowledge. He linked power with education and made this clear, that education is the only remedy for the economic, social and political wretched condition of Muslims. He made it clear that Muslims, only by being adorned with modern education, can get deliverance from the dominance of the English and the Hindus. He laid the foundation of the concept of a separate Islamic state. He prepared the Muslims of the Subcontinent to become united for the establishment of a separate Islamic state, so that all their affairs could be settled in the light of the Quran and Sunnah.

In 1885, after the foundation of the Congress, most Muslim leaders joined it, but afterwards this matter became clear to them that the Congress is a representative party only of the Hindus. At that time the need was felt for a separate political party for Muslims. In 1906 the Muslim League came into existence, which later came forth as the sole representative party of Muslims. Mawlana Hasrat Mohani presented a plan in which the division of the Subcontinent into two states was spoken of.

paras.text: … made the establishment of Pakistan inevitable. Islam alone became the basis of the ideology of Pakistan. Addressing a session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad, Allama Iqbal for the first time presented the concept of a separate Islamic state. This is the reason that Allama Iqbal is also called the Poet-Philosopher who conceived Pakistan.

paras.text: From 1937 Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah (who was the possessor of a great personality) took up the responsibility of the struggle for a separate country for Muslims. … made the establishment of Pakistan inevitable. Islam alone became the basis of the ideology of Pakistan. Addressing a session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad, Allama Iqbal for the first time presented the concept of a separate Islamic state. This is the reason that Allama Iqbal is also called the Poet-Philosopher who conceived Pakistan.

From 1937 Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah (who was the possessor of a great personality) took up the responsibility of the struggle for a separate country for Muslims. He united all the Muslims of the Subcontinent and made this matter clear to them, that the Muslim never gets perturbed in adversity. This was the reason that the Muslims of Hindustan chose the Quaid-e-Azam as their leader and responded "labbayk" to his every word.

After the coming of the Quaid-e-Azam, the Pakistan Movement gained popularity very quickly and crossed all stages of success. He made it clear that the designs of the Congress have left no other way for Muslims except that they struggle for the establishment of a separate free Islamic state. On 23 March 1940, in the annual session of the Muslim League at Lahore, the Pakistan Resolution was passed.

After a tireless movement brimming with the spirit of self-sacrifice, ultimately on 14 August 1947 Pakistan came into existence as an Islamic state.

The political situation of Pakistan

At the time of the partition of Hindustan the English left some such defects which caused severe harm to the progress and political stability of Pakistan. For this very reason two wars, in 1948 and 1965, have been fought with Hindustan only because of the issue of Kashmir. All the rivers flowing in Pakistan pass through occupied Kashmir. In 1960, in the Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan had to wash its hands of three rivers, the Ravi, the Beas and the Sutlej, whereas Pakistan's right to the rivers Indus, Chenab and Jhelum was recognised.

In 1948 the Quaid-e-Azam passed away. After him the government came into the hands of Liaquat Ali Khan. In 1951 Liaquat Ali Khan was martyred. From 1951 to 1958 many governments came and ended. In 1956 the first constitution was enforced in Pakistan. Despite this, the result of the political crisis was that in 1958 martial law was imposed in Pakistan.
